preconditions.description: The number of vertices n and queries q are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n and all(0 <= x <= n for x in a)
preconditions.description: The list of vertex values a has length n, and each value is between 0 and n inclusive.
There are exactly n-1 edges defining the tree structure.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints are valid vertex indices between 1 and n.
The number of queries matches q.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in queries)
preconditions.description: All query endpoints are valid vertex indices between 1 and n.
The input edges form a valid tree rooted at vertex 1, and for every query (u, v), u is an ancestor of v.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(int(output_lines[i]) == max((a[path_idx - 1] ^ (dist_to_v - dist_to_v + dist_to_v)) for path_idx in path_indices) for i, (u, v) in enumerate(queries))
postconditions.description: This clause is syntactically invalid due to the complexity of defining 'path' and 'dist' purely in a single expression without helper definitions. Re-evaluating to use a semantic helper definition approach as permitted.
